key_insight: Feasibility alone is not enough: for constrained QAOA, the shallow circuit can only reach a finite-depth accessible set, and the quality of that reachable set predicts performance better than global mixer connectivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, parameter-independent way to judge whether a constrained QAOA design is worth its qubit and depth budget before running expensive optimization.
method: Define the finite-depth accessible set R_p(M,x0) for a chosen feasible start state, mixer schedule, and circuit depth.
Upper-bound achievable objective quality with f_R^* = max_{x in R_p} f(x) and normalize it as reachable-quality Q_R.
Test block-local XY mixer schedules on constrained portfolio optimization and synthetic block-constrained quadratic problems, including compilation-cost analysis.
evidence_signal: Across 207 favorable-tail CVaR QAOA configurations, Q_R had the strongest association with realized shallow-QAOA performance among the structural diagnostics, with Pearson 0.7003 and Spearman 0.8057 correlations.
watch_item: The accessible-set diagnostic depends on the specific initial state, finite depth, and compiled mixer/phase-separator routing, so results may change substantially under different circuit synthesis choices or hardware constraints.
paper_title: Beyond Feasibility: Finite-Depth Accessibility in Constrained QAOA
